description: Source-grounded 50-question multi-hop set on the documented May 2017 WannaCry impact on the NHS in England.
trusted_context: This trusted context is restricted to the local NAO, DHSC, CISA/US-CERT, Microsoft MS17-010, and checksum sources listed in the source manifest. nw_f001: WannaCry attack on the NHS affected trusts total at least 80 of 236 trusts. Evidence: NAO says at least 80 out of 236 trusts across England were affected. nw_f002: at least 80 of 236 trusts included infected locked trusts 34 infected and locked out trusts. Evidence: Of the 80 affected trusts, 34 were infected and locked out of devices. nw_f003: 34 infected and locked out trusts included acute trusts 25 infected acute trusts. Evidence: The 34 infected and locked-out trusts included 25 acute trusts. nw_f004: 25 infected acute trusts had diverting subset five acute trusts that diverted emergency ambulance services. Evidence: Of the 25 infected acute trusts, five had to divert emergency ambulance services. nw_f005: five acute trusts that diverted emergency ambulance services included trust Barts Health NHS Trust. Evidence: Barts Health NHS Trust was one of the five trusts listed as diverting emergency ambulance services. nw_f006: Barts Health NHS Trust diverted hospital Royal London Hospital. Evidence: The listed Barts Health site was Royal London Hospital. nw_f007: Royal London Hospital diverted service type emergency ambulance services. Evidence: The listed hospitals were associated with diverted emergency ambulance services. nw_f008: emergency ambulance services patient consequence patients had to travel further. Evidence: NAO says some patients had to travel further because five hospitals diverted services. nw_f009: patients had to travel further unknown measure number of diverted ambulances and patients. Evidence: NAO says data were not collected on how many ambulances and patients were diverted. nw_f010: number of diverted ambulances and patients data collection status not collected by NHS England. Evidence: NHS England did not collect data on diverted ambulances and patients. nw_f011: WannaCry attack on the NHS infected primary care and other orgs 603 primary care and other NHS organisations. Evidence: NAO says 603 primary care and other NHS organisations were infected. nw_f012: 603 primary care and other NHS organisations included gp practices 595 GP practices. Evidence: The 603 infected primary care and other organisations included 595 GP practices. nw_f013: 595 GP practices needed machines rebuilt before patch deployment. Evidence: The DHSC review says 595 infected practices needed machines rebuilt before they were patched. nw_f014: patch deployment ninety five percent completed by 17 May 2017. Evidence: The DHSC review says 95% of infected practices were re-installed and patched by 17 May. nw_f015: 17 May 2017 remaining five percent completed by Friday 19 May 2017. Evidence: The remaining 5% were completed by Friday 19 May when the incident was stood down. nw_f016: Friday 19 May 2017 incident status stood down. Evidence: The DHSC review says the incident was stood down on Friday 19 May 2017. nw_f017: stood down time 5:30 pm. Evidence: NAO Figure 2 records the incident stood down at 5:30 pm on Friday 19 May. nw_f018: stood down authority NHS England. Evidence: NAO Figure 2 says the incident was stood down by NHS England. nw_f019: NHS England worked with IT suppliers of GP practices. Evidence: NAO Figure 2 says NHS England worked with IT suppliers of GP practices to patch GP IT systems. nw_f020: IT suppliers of GP practices included commissioning support units or private-sector support. Evidence: NAO Figure 2 identifies commissioning support units or private-sector support as GP-practice IT suppliers. nw_f021: WannaCry attack on the NHS exploited vulnerability common Windows operating system vulnerability. Evidence: NHS Digital told NAO that infected trusts had a common Windows operating-system vulnerability exploited by WannaCry. nw_f022: common Windows operating system vulnerability affected systems status unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems. Evidence: All infected NHS organisations had unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems. nw_f023: unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems majority infected devices supported Windows 7. Evidence: NHS Digital told NAO the majority of infected NHS devices were unpatched but on supported Windows 7. nw_f024: supported Windows 7 protected by Microsoft March 2017 patch. Evidence: Trusts using Windows 7 could have protected themselves by applying a Microsoft patch issued in March 2017. nw_f025: Microsoft March 2017 patch bulletin MS17-010. Evidence: Microsoft identifies MS17-010 as the March 2017 security bulletin for this SMB server update. nw_f026: MS17-010 publication date 14 March 2017. Evidence: Microsoft lists the bulletin as published on March 14, 2017. nw_f027: MS17-010 severity Critical. Evidence: Microsoft titles the bulletin Critical and rates the update Critical for supported Windows releases. nw_f028: MS17-010 component SMBv1 server. Evidence: Microsoft says the severe vulnerability concerned Microsoft Server Message Block 1.0 (SMBv1) server. nw_f029: SMBv1 server attack condition specially crafted messages. Evidence: Remote code execution could occur if an attacker sent specially crafted messages to an SMBv1 server. nw_f030: specially crafted messages worst impact remote code execution. Evidence: Microsoft describes remote code execution as the most severe impact. nw_f031: WannaCry attack on the NHS preparedness assessment CareCERT Assure. Evidence: Before WannaCry, NHS Digital offered an on-site cyber-security assessment known as CareCERT Assure. nw_f032: CareCERT Assure offered by NHS Digital. Evidence: NHS Digital offered CareCERT Assure before the attack. nw_f033: CareCERT Assure format on-site cyber-security assessment. Evidence: CareCERT Assure was an on-site inspection to assess hospital cyber-security. nw_f034: CareCERT Assure participating trusts before attack 88 of 236 trusts. Evidence: By 12 May, NHS Digital had inspected 88 out of 236 trusts. nw_f035: 88 of 236 trusts pass result none passed. Evidence: None of the 88 inspected trusts had passed. nw_f036: none passed assessment date context before 12 May 2017. Evidence: The CareCERT Assure pass result is stated for the period before 12 May 2017. nw_f037: before 12 May 2017 department mechanism status no formal compliance assessment mechanism. Evidence: Before 12 May, no formal mechanism existed for assessing CareCERT-alert compliance. nw_f038: no formal compliance assessment mechanism assessed compliance with NHS advice and guidance. Evidence: NAO says the Department had no formal mechanism for assessing compliance with its advice and guidance before 12 May. nw_f039: NHS advice and guidance included alerts CareCERT alerts. Evidence: The compliance gap included NHS Digital CareCERT alerts warning organisations to patch systems. nw_f040: CareCERT alerts requested action software patches. Evidence: NAO describes CareCERT alerts as including applying software patches and keeping antivirus up to date. nw_f041: WannaCry attack on the NHS infected device majority unpatched supported Windows 7 devices. Evidence: NAO says unsupported XP devices were in the minority of identified issues. nw_f043: unsupported Windows XP devices estate share on 12 may about 5% of NHS IT estate. Evidence: The Department told NAO that about 5% of the NHS IT estate was still using Windows XP on 12 May 2017. nw_f044: about 5% of NHS IT estate included computers and medical equipment. Evidence: The 5% XP estate included computers and medical equipment. nw_f045: computers and medical equipment medical equipment example MRI scanners. Evidence: NAO cites MRI scanners as medical equipment with Windows XP embedded. nw_f046: MRI scanners could be protected by isolating devices from rest of network. Evidence: Trusts running Windows XP on medical equipment could have protected themselves by isolating those devices from the network. nw_f047: isolating devices from rest of network may require manual workarounds. Evidence: NAO says isolating such devices may necessitate manual workarounds. nw_f048: manual workarounds recording method pen and paper records. Evidence: Some disrupted trusts used manual workarounds and recorded information using pen and paper. nw_f049: pen and paper records disruption context trusts not infected but reporting disruption. Evidence: NAO describes manual workarounds among disruption at trusts not infected by the ransomware. nw_f050: trusts not infected but reporting disruption count 46 trusts. Evidence: Of the 80 affected trusts, 46 were not infected but reported disruption. nw_f051: WannaCry attack on the NHS global computers affected more than 200,000 computers. Evidence: NAO says WannaCry affected more than 200,000 computers globally. nw_f052: WannaCry attack on the NHS global country scope at least 100 countries. Evidence: NAO says the global attack affected at least 100 countries. nw_f053: WannaCry attack on the NHS nhs targeting status NHS was not the specific target. Evidence: NAO says the NHS was particularly affected but was not the specific target. nw_f054: WannaCry attack on the NHS affected services week 12 May to 19 May 2017. Evidence: NAO says NHS services were affected in the week from 12 May to 19 May 2017. nw_f055: WannaCry attack on the NHS major incident declared by NHS England. Evidence: NHS England declared the cyber attack a major incident. nw_f056: NHS England declared major incident at 4 pm on 12 May 2017. Evidence: NAO states the major incident was declared at 4 pm on 12 May. nw_f057: NHS England initiated eprr at 6:45 pm on 12 May 2017. Evidence: NAO says NHS England initiated EPRR plans at 6:45 pm. nw_f058: NHS England coordinated with key partner NHS Digital. Evidence: NAO Figure 2 says NHS England led the response, coordinating particularly with NHS Digital. nw_f059: WannaCry attack on the NHS kill switch activated evening of 12 May 2017. Evidence: The cyber-security researcher triggered the kill-switch on the evening of Friday 12 May. nw_f060: kill-switch effect WannaCry stopped locking devices. Evidence: NAO says the kill-switch meant WannaCry stopped locking devices. nw_f061: WannaCry attack on the NHS ransom payment status no NHS organisation paid the ransom. Evidence: The Department, NHS England and NCA told NAO no NHS organisations paid the ransom. nw_f062: NHS Digital advised against payment of the WannaCry ransom. Evidence: NHS Digital advised against paying the WannaCry ransom during visits and calls. nw_f063: NHS England and NHS Digital wrote to all trusts on 14 May 2017. Evidence: NHS England and NHS Digital wrote to all trusts on 14 May advising against paying ransoms. nw_f064: WannaCry attack on the NHS identified cancelled appointments 6,912 appointments. Evidence: NHS England identified 6,912 cancelled appointments. nw_f065: WannaCry attack on the NHS estimated total cancelled appointments around 19,494 appointments. Evidence: NHS England estimated total cancelled appointments at around 19,494. nw_f066: 6,912 appointments excluded repeat outpatient appointments and later cancellations. Evidence: The identified 6,912 did not include repeat outpatient appointments or cancellations identified after 18 May. nw_f067: around 19,494 appointments basis normal rate of follow-up appointments to first appointments. Evidence: The estimate was based on the normal rate of follow-up appointments to first appointments. nw_f068: WannaCry attack on the NHS urgent cancer referrals cancelled by 18 may at least 139 patients. Evidence: NHS England identified at least 139 patients with urgent referrals for potential cancer cancelled as at 18 May. nw_f069: WannaCry attack on the NHS diagnostic equipment infected as of 19 may 1,220 pieces of diagnostic equipment. Evidence: As at 19 May 2017, NHS England had identified 1,220 pieces of diagnostic equipment infected. nw_f070: 1,220 pieces of diagnostic equipment proportion of such equipment 1%. Evidence: NAO says the 1,220 infected pieces were 1% of all such NHS equipment. nw_f071: diagnostic equipment disruption affected departments radiology and pathology departments. Evidence: Locked or isolated medical equipment disrupted radiology and pathology departments. nw_f072: diagnostic equipment disruption diagnostic imaging example MRI scanners. Evidence: NAO names MRI scanners as diagnostic imaging equipment affected by locking or isolation. nw_f073: WannaCry attack on the NHS patient harm reports no reported cases of patient harm. Evidence: NHS organisations did not report cases of patient harm. nw_f074: WannaCry attack on the NHS patient data reports no reported compromise or theft of patient data. Evidence: NHS organisations did not report patient data compromised or stolen. nw_f075: national NHS IT systems managed by NHS Digital not infected example NHS Spine. Evidence: NAO identifies NHSmail as the NHS email system. nw_f079: WannaCry attack on the NHS spread via internet including N3 network. Evidence: NHS Digital confirmed there were no instances of the ransomware spreading via NHSmail. nw_f081: N3 network network description broadband network connecting all NHS sites in England. Evidence: NAO describes N3 as the broadband network connecting all NHS sites in England. nw_f082: WannaCry attack on the NHS domain contacting trusts not locked 21 trusts. Evidence: NHS England and NHS Digital identified 21 trusts attempting to contact the WannaCry domain but not locked out. nw_f083: WannaCry attack on the NHS later domain contacting organisations 92 organisations. Evidence: Between 15 May and mid-September, 92 organisations were identified attempting to contact the WannaCry domain. nw_f084: 92 organisations included 21 trusts. Evidence: The later 92 organisations included 21 trusts. nw_f085: 34 infected and locked out trusts regional concentration 29 in North NHS region and Midlands and East NHS region. Evidence: North Cumbria University Hospitals NHS Trust was one of the five listed diverting trusts. nw_f094: North Cumbria University Hospitals NHS Trust diverted hospital West Cumberland Hospital. Evidence: The listed North Cumbria site was West Cumberland Hospital. nw_f095: Tuesday 16 May 2017 remaining diverting hospitals Lister Hospital and Broomfield Hospital. Evidence: By Tuesday 16 May only Lister Hospital and Broomfield Hospital were still diverting patients. nw_f096: Department and Cabinet Office 2014 letter told trusts to have robust plans to migrate away from Windows XP. Evidence: The Department and Cabinet Office wrote in 2014 that robust plans to migrate away from Windows XP were essential. nw_f097: robust plans to migrate away from Windows XP deadline context April 2015. Evidence: The 2014 letter offered temporary help until April 2015, after which there would be no support. nw_f098: NHS Digital cannot mandate local remedial action. Evidence: NHS Digital cannot mandate a local body to take remedial action. nw_f099: CareCERT Assure voluntary status voluntary inspection. Evidence: CareCERT Assure inspection was voluntary. nw_f100: CareCERT alerts first patch alert date 17 March 2017. Evidence: NHS Digital issued a CareCERT alert on 17 March asking trusts to apply the patch. nw_f101: CareCERT alerts second patch alert date 28 April 2017. Evidence: NHS Digital issued a CareCERT alert on 28 April asking trusts to apply the patch. nw_f102: NHS England and NHS Improvement post attack letter recipients every trust, clinical commissioning group and commissioning support unit. Evidence: After WannaCry, NHS England and NHS Improvement wrote to every trust, CCG and CSU. nw_f103: post-attack board assurance request covered all 39 CareCERT alerts issued between March and May 2017. Evidence: The post-attack request asked boards to ensure all 39 CareCERT alerts from March to May were implemented. nw_f104: post-attack board assurance request also covered essential action to secure local firewalls. Evidence: The same request asked boards to ensure essential action to secure local firewalls. nw_f105: internet-facing firewall management would have guarded against infection even if systems were unpatched. Evidence: NAO states managing firewalls facing the internet would have guarded organisations against infection whether patched or not. nw_f106: Department of Health overall responsibility health sector cyber-security resilience and incident response. Evidence: NAO says the Department and NHS England worked with NHS Improvement and others to respond. nw_f112: affected trusts communication workaround WhatsApp on personal mobile devices. Evidence: The reviews warned that cyber attacks could put patient information at risk and jeopardise access to critical patient record systems. nw_f116: Department formal response to reviews published July 2017.
